newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut shares fall on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Beirut shares fall on profit-taking.

text.p: Solidere B shares and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce fell on profit-taking on the Beirut Stock Exchange for the second successive day, dealers said.
BLC fell to $16.75 from $17 and Solidere B shares fell to $11.375 from $11.75. Solidere A shares were unchanged at $11.5.
"What is going on is just a matter of profit-taking which increased supply, I do not think it is a trend," Hayssam Arabi, a broker for Middle East Capital Group, told Reuters.
BLC reported on Monday first quarter consolidated pre-tax profits of 8.04 billion Lebanese pounds ($5.2 million). Financiers called the results "very good" and in line with expectations.
The two other listed banks, Banque Audi and Bank of Beirut, were unchanged at $20 and $3.5625 respectively.
The BLC fall dragged the LIBX bank index down 0.49 percent to 138.10. The LISPI and BLOM general indices fell 0.33 percent and 0.96 percent to 87.5 and 985.64 respectively.
Total BSE turnover was 201,666 shares for a value of $2,144,311 compared with 203,310 shares and $1,954,167 on Monday.
There was no trade in the four listed industrial companies: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
